is_anopheles.evidence: Four strains of An. gambiae s.l. mosquitoes were used in the experiments: Kisumu, N'gousso, Banfora, and VK7 (Page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study mentions that the Banfora and VK7 laboratory strains have a high frequency of 1014F kdr citing previous literature (ref 25), but does not genotype target markers in this study (Page 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts or frequencies with sample size are reported for target markers.

african_field_population.evidence: All bioassays were performed using long-established laboratory colonies (Kisumu, N'gousso, VK7, Banfora) maintained at LSTM; no field populations were collected or tested (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical laboratory study characterizing adaptations to the WHO cone test (Page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: No field collection locations are reported as only laboratory colony strains were used.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection years are reported for mosquito samples in this study.

duplicate_risk.evidence: No field genotype data were presented.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary genotype data are needed as the study is ineligible based on criteria checks.

assessment.summary: This laboratory study evaluated adaptations to the WHO cone bioassay (adding a human host attractant and video tracking) to measure behavioural responses and post-exposure effects in four colony strains of Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Kisumu, N'gousso, Banfora, VK7). No field collections or target marker genotyping were conducted.
exclusion_reasons: No target markers genotyped in this study
Only laboratory colonies used; no African field populations tested
